children: Gold prices are broadly muted, hovering around $4,300 a troy ounce as expectations that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates further weigh on the nonyielding asset. In early European trading, futures in New York are flat at $4,316.30 an ounce, pressured by a stronger dollar and Treasury yields climbing to multi-year highs. "Fed officials have also maintained a hawkish stance, with Governor Michael Barr indicating that further tightening may be required," analysts at MUFG say. "With markets now pricing at least three additional hikes by April, elevated yields and persistent energy-driven inflation remain significant headwinds for noninterest-bearing gold." (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
